summary: The milestone-scoped timing detector reported 0 commits since activation, so the locked fields are total_wall_time_minutes=0, experiments_completed=0, compute_bound_experiments_count=0. This is NOT an empty milestone: it is the recurring false-zero observability gap documented across prior operational retros (the milestone's experiments ran and landed on disk; the detector under-reports them to the retro TIMING DATA block). With no monitored-3090 compute-bound task in the milestone, the 0% GPU utilization in the GPU report is correct idle, so gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is null.
bottlenecks_identified: RECURRING (highest-leverage): the milestone-scoped timing detector false-reported 0 commits since activation. The same false-zero gap has been documented for many consecutive prior milestones. Because the retro TIMING DATA block is fed by this detector, the operational retro receives no authoritative per-experiment timing — the locked 0/0/0 reflect the detector, not the milestone's real execution.

A long-running held-out-score arm exceeded the experiment agent's wall-clock cap and its artifact did not land in time, causing the milestone capstone to record honest_verdict=blocked_upstream_artifacts on a missing upstream arm. A checkpoint/resume + soft-budget fix was applied during the milestone so the score survives the cap.

Housekeeping (not a wall-time bottleneck): an idle Python process (PID 3095366) holds 536MB on GPU 0 at 0% utilization — a possible leaked/idle allocation to reclaim before the next milestone's compute-bound tasks.
improvements_suggested: Move the existing detector-wire to the conductor's retro TIMING-DATA prompt-assembly call site so the retro consumes real commit/timing data, AND add a disk-mtime fallback so a detector false-zero degrades to a verifiable artifact-mtime window instead of reporting an empty milestone.

Make held-out / long-running scoring tasks checkpoint/resume by default with a soft wall-clock budget, so a task that exceeds the agent cap resumes rather than leaving the capstone blocked on a missing upstream artifact.
Stamp duration_s, inference_substrate, and a compute_bound flag at artifact write time, so the retro can classify GPU-idle correctness without re-deriving substrate from markers.
Free the idle GPU-0 allocation (PID 3095366, 536MB, 0% util) so both RTX 3090s start the next milestone clean.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix the false-zero timing detector: wire it into the conductor's retro prompt-assembly call site and add a disk-mtime fallback, so future operational retros reflect real execution instead of a phantom empty milestone.
Default long-running held-out-score arms to checkpoint/resume with a soft wall-clock budget, eliminating the blocked_upstream_artifacts capstone outcome caused by the agent wall-clock cap.
Add write-time duration_s/inference_substrate/compute_bound stamping plus reclaim the idle GPU-0 process, so GPU-efficiency analysis is mechanical and both 3090s are free for compute-bound work.
meta_reflection: The retro's own input was corrupted by the long-recurring false-zero observability gap, so the most important operational finding this milestone is again diagnostic, not per-experiment: the milestone executed cleanly (a bridge-not-crossed null plus one banked self-play level), but the detector reported nothing. With no monitored-3090 compute-bound task, the idle GPUs are correct and carry no efficiency lesson; fixing the detector wire and defaulting long scoring arms to checkpoint/resume are the overdue, highest-leverage changes.
